**Analysis of the test image:**

**Plant part affected**: Tomato leaves (upper surface visible)

**Key visual features observed**:
- Numerous small, dark brown to black spots scattered across the leaf surface
- Spots appear angular/irregular in shape (not perfectly circular)
- Some spots show slight yellowish halos around them
- Leaf margins display some browning/yellowing
- Spots are very small (pinpoint to ~1/8 inch), not large bullseye-type lesions
- No tan/gray centers with pycnidia (ruling out Septoria)
- No concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight)
- No velvety mold growth visible (ruling out Leaf Mold)
- No bronze discoloration pattern (ruling out TSWV)

**Differential reasoning**:
- The small, dark (nearly black), angular spots with yellow halos are the hallmark of **Bacterial Speck of Tomato**
- Septoria Leaf Blotch would show circular lesions with tan/gray centers and visible dark pycnidia — not seen here
- The spots are uniformly dark (not tan-centered), angular, and surrounded by chlorotic halos, matching Bacterial Speck perfectly
- Early Blight would show larger, concentric-ringed dark lesions — not present here

The spots are uniformly dark without tan/gray centers (ruling out Septoria), lack concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight), and show no velvety fungal growth (ruling out Leaf Mold or Gray Mold)."}
